number.why: The source explicitly reports RR 0.49 (95% CI 0.24–0.65) for colchicine versus placebo and identifies recurrent pericarditis as the primary ITT outcome. However, the reported estimate is not explicitly linked to the served timepoint, 'longest reported recurrence follow-up'. The registry specifies a protocol outcome at 18 months, which does not establish the reported estimate's timepoint or that it is the longest follow-up. Thus the printed numbers agree, but complete confirmation of the served outcome is not established.

quotes.span: The primary outcome was recurrent pericarditis in the intention-to-treat population.

The proportion of patients who had recurrent pericarditis was 26 (21·6%) of 120 in the colchicine group and 51 (42·5%) of 120 in the placebo group (relative risk 0·49; 95% CI 0·24-0·65; p=0·0009; number needed to treat 5).
PROTOCOL PRIMARY OUTCOME: Recurrence rate at 18 months |  | TIME FRAME: 18 m onths

entry.why: Adults with multiple recurrences are explicitly included in the question. The source establishes that population and the randomized, double-blind comparison of colchicine added to conventional anti-inflammatory treatment versus placebo.

quotes.span: We did this multicentre, double-blind trial at four general hospitals in northern Italy.

Adult patients with multiple recurrences of pericarditis (≥two) were randomly assigned (1:1) to placebo or colchicine (0·5 mg twice daily for 6 months for patients weighing more than 70 kg or 0·5 mg once daily for patients weighing 70 kg or less) in addition to conventional anti-inflammatory treatment with aspirin, ibuprofen, or indometacin.

missed: The ruling acknowledges the unresolved follow-up binding but still declares SERVED_CONFIRMED. Also, the quoted arm counts imply a crude RR of (26/120)/(51/120) = 0.5098039; 0.4901961 is the corresponding relative risk reduction. This discrepancy warrants distinguishing the explicitly printed 'relative risk' from a validated risk-ratio estimand. The packet does not explain the discrepancy, so it does not justify relabeling or replacing the published estimate and CI.
